mechanism_narrative: The sustained four-week trend of increasing RETAIL_REC mobility, moving from -39.6% to -21.3%, indicates a continuous easing of restrictions or behavioral shift. This positive momentum will persist and drive further increases in retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rebound in WORKPLACES mobility, increasing from -31.4% to -23.0% in the last week, indicates a return to office-based work. This directly translates to increased foot traffic in retail and recreation areas during weekdays over the next four weeks, as people combine work with leisure.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES mobility increases by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase despite WORKPLACES mobility rising by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The combined effect of decreasing RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 16.0% to 8.4%) and increasing GROCERY_PHARM mobility (from -6.7% to -1.3%) suggests a broader comfort with public spaces and a return to out-of-home routines. This will spill over into non-essential retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days decreases, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility falling and GROCERY_PHARM mobility rising.

mechanism_narrative: As public health policies ease, the sustained increase in TRANSIT station usage (from -66.0% to -54.1%), despite still being low, reflects a growing confidence in public transport. This is a prerequisite for a broader return to retail and recreation activities over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase, even if TRANSIT mobility continues its upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility over the past four weeks (from 16.0% to 8.4%) indicates a sustained shift away from staying at home. This frees up time and willingness for out-of-home activities, including retail and recreation, leading to an increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility continuing to decline.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM mobility approaches baseline levels (currently -1.3%, within 2 percentage points of baseline), it signifies a return to pre-pandemic essential shopping habits. This often precedes or coincides with a rebound in non-essential retail and recreation within the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM mobility is less than -2 percentage points from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days does not increase, despite GROCERY_PHARM mobility being within 2 percentage points of baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent and sustained increase in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility (WORKPLACES from -35.3% to -23.0%, TRANSIT from -66.0% to -54.1%) suggests a coordinated return to daily routines involving commuting. This directly boosts foot traffic in retail and recreation areas, particularly during lunch breaks and after-work hours, over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases, despite both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility showing sustained increases.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, if PARKS mobility remains low or decreases (currently -14.0%) while other categories rise, it implies people are shifting from outdoor, socially distanced activities to indoor, commercial recreation. This behavioral shift will drive RETAIL_REC up over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility is below -10 percentage points from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days decreases, despite PARKS mobility remaining low (below -10%) and other mobility categories increasing.
